slides.say: x is a two-digit number. x is equal to the cube of its units digit, plus four times the sum of its digits. What is the tens digit of x?

slides: This digit puzzle is written in words, so first we turn the words into an equation. We need the tens digit of x. [short pause] We'll solve it two ways, writing the number with its digits, and then testing the answer choices.

slides.say: [short pause] Let's call the tens digit T and the ones digit U. A two-digit number is ten times its tens digit, plus its ones digit, so x is ten T plus U. The sum of its digits is T plus U.
at: so x is ten T plus U

slides.say: Now the words of the question. The cube of the units digit is U cubed. Four times the sum of the digits is four times the whole bracket, T plus U. So x equals U cubed, plus four times the bracket T plus U. The four multiplies both digits, not just T.

Both expressions equal x, so we set them equal. Ten T plus U equals U cubed plus four T plus four U. Now subtract four T and U from both sides. On the left, ten T minus four T leaves six T. On the right, four U minus U leaves three U. So six T equals U cubed plus three U.

T is a digit, so it's at most nine, and six T is at most fifty-four. Can U be zero? Then U cubed plus three U is zero, so six T is zero, and T is zero. But T is the tens digit, and a two-digit number can't start with zero. So U isn't zero, and we test U from one.

U is one gives one plus three, which is four. U is two gives eight plus six, which is fourteen. U is three gives twenty-seven plus nine, which is thirty-six. U is four gives sixty-four plus twelve, which is seventy-six, already more than fifty-four. A bigger U only makes U cubed plus three U bigger, so we can stop.
Four and fourteen are not six times a digit, but thirty-six is. Six T is thirty-six, so T is six. Choice number three is our answer.
at: Choice number three is our answer

slides.say: [pause] Now let's test the answer choices. Each choice gives a possible tens digit T, and then we need a digit U that fits the words of the question. Start with choice number one, seven. Then x is seventy plus U, and its digit sum is seven plus U. So seventy plus U must equal U cubed plus twenty-eight plus four U. Subtract twenty-eight and U from both sides, and U cubed plus three U must be forty-two.
at: U cubed plus three U must be forty-two

slides.say: U is three gives twenty-seven plus nine, which is thirty-six, and U is four gives sixty-four plus twelve, which is seventy-six. As U grows, U cubed plus three U only grows, so it jumps from thirty-six straight to seventy-six. Forty-two is in between, so no digit U works, and choice number one is out.
at: and choice number one is out

slides.say: The other tens digits work the same way. T is five needs U cubed plus three U to be thirty, and T is four needs it to be twenty-four. U is two gives only fourteen, and U is three already gives thirty-six. Thirty and twenty-four are in between, so no digit works, and choice numbers two and four are out.

T is six needs thirty-six, and U is three gives exactly that. So x is sixty-three. Let's check it in the words of the question. The units digit is three, and three cubed is twenty-seven. The digit sum is nine, and four times nine is thirty-six. Twenty-seven plus thirty-six is sixty-three. It fits, so choice number three is our answer. [pause] Okay. I'll see you in the next question.
